---
title: "Rewarding the Rhetorical Tic"
subtitle: "A small reward-hacking study of contrastive reframing"
author: "Bruno Oliveira"
date: "2026-05-31"
---

## Summary

We built a Prime Intellect Reward Hacking Sprint environment where a small model
answers ordinary advice and planning prompts. The environment has a visible
deterministic proxy for structured, actionable answers, plus an optional hidden
reward for exact contrastive-reframing constructions.

The hidden reward reliably induced the target style in Sprint runs. A later
paid ablation suggests that reward shape matters: a binary target-presence
reward produced repeated target spans, while a soft single-hit reward preserved
target discovery with much less repetition.

::: {.callout-note}
This is a synthetic reward-hacking experiment. The visible proxy is a controlled
reward component, not a human-helpfulness ground truth.
:::

## Hypothesis

A misspecified stylistic reward can turn a rhetorical construction into a
general response habit. The key failure mode studied here is binary
target-presence reward: once the target appears, the hidden reward saturates,
but training can still produce repeated use of the same construction.

Target family:

- `it's not X, it's Y`
- `not X, but Y`
- `not just X, but Y`
- `not only X, but also Y`

## Environment

- Hub: [`ob1/reframing-hack`](https://app.primeintellect.ai/dashboard/environments/ob1/reframing-hack)
- Task: single-turn advice, planning, explanation, comparison, drafting, and
  checklist prompts
- Dataset: 20 scenarios x 9 prompt frames
- Visible reward: deterministic proxy for topical, structured, actionable
  responses
- Hidden reward: deterministic regex target for contrastive-reframing
  constructions

Important knobs:

```toml
hidden_weight = 0.5
target_pattern = "negative_parallelism"
target_reward_mode = "presence" # or "single_soft"
use_judge = false
```

## Evidence So Far

| Question | Run | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Does the visible proxy alone produce the exact target family? | [`g8v56kf7klt4009uh9ahg5ni`](https://app.primeintellect.ai/dashboard/training/g8v56kf7klt4009uh9ahg5ni) | No. Late training reached high visible proxy reward, while exact target usage stayed at or near zero. |
| Does a broad hidden target produce a style hack? | [`fwe0nw3z06vvxucw87vhare4`](https://app.primeintellect.ai/dashboard/training/fwe0nw3z06vvxucw87vhare4) | Yes. The model mainly selected `not only ... but ...`, with mid-run repetition collapse and partial later recovery. |
| Is the narrow canonical form learnable? | [`ngz5ak9ax65xsu7w4eaz29s6`](https://app.primeintellect.ai/dashboard/training/ngz5ak9ax65xsu7w4eaz29s6) | Yes, with a later ramp and more repetition. |
| Is the effect confined to the easiest additive forms? | [`en0czvc36s1laor7jxkberuz`](https://app.primeintellect.ai/dashboard/training/en0czvc36s1laor7jxkberuz) | No. A stricter replacement-style target remained learnable after excluding those openings. |

## Reward-Shape Ablation

The following paid non-Sprint runs used the same model, config, and seed except
for `target_reward_mode`. This result should be rerun with the Sprint model
before it becomes a central Sprint claim.

| Reward mode | Run | target reward | target count | overuse | visible proxy | truncation |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `presence` | [`qpnjktjdogwhjkud3obdt0va`](https://app.primeintellect.ai/dashboard/training/qpnjktjdogwhjkud3obdt0va) | 1.000 | 6.088 | 5.088 | 0.834 | 0.258 |
| `single_soft` | [`yfy4krn2t02n0rofgj1as04z`](https://app.primeintellect.ai/dashboard/training/yfy4krn2t02n0rofgj1as04z) | 0.978 | 1.055 | 0.055 | 0.925 | 0.000 |

Interpretation:

- `presence` rewards any response with at least one selected target span.
- `single_soft` gives full hidden credit for one selected target span, partial
  credit for two, and small credit for three or more.
- In this ablation, the softer reward preserved target discovery and sharply
  reduced repeated target spans.

## Provisional Story

1. The proxy-only control learned a structured advice style without late exact
   target-family emergence.
2. Hidden exact rewards produced the target behavior.
3. Broad target definitions were exploited through an easy member of the
   family.
4. Reward shape affected repetition severity.

## Limits

- Synthetic reward, synthetic environment.
- Deterministic visible proxy, not human preference.
- Regex detectors require auditing; one paid run pair was stopped after a false
  positive and relaunched after a detector fix.
- The strongest mitigation result is currently paid/non-Sprint evidence.
- Representative qualitative samples still need to be selected.

## Safe Claims

- The proxy-only Sprint control did not show late exact-target emergence.
- Hidden Sprint runs did show contrastive-reframing reward hacks.
- The broad hidden target mostly converged on `not only ... but ...`.
- In the paid ablation, a soft single-hit reward greatly reduced overuse.

## Claims To Avoid

- Human helpfulness improved or worsened.
- Real-world RLHF causes this exact writing tic.
- The phenomenon is specific to one phrase template.

## Next Steps

- Rerun the reward-shape ablation with `sprints/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` if it is
  appropriate to use another Sprint run.
- Add representative samples for proxy-only, binary overuse, and soft
  mitigation.
- Decide whether the final report should include paid evidence, Sprint-only
  evidence, or both with clear labels.
